questions.title: What if your ball rolls out of the right place after you drop it?
questions.question: You drop your ball in the spot you should. But the ball rolls out of the area you can use. What should you do now?

choices.text: Drop the ball again inside the area you are allowed
Put the ball down with your hand where it stopped
Hit the ball from where it ended up
Move the ball back to the first place you dropped it

questions.explanation: If your ball rolls out of the area after you drop it, you have to drop it again inside the right area.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The special part of the ground where you are allowed to drop and play your ball from.
Letting the ball go from your hand so it falls to the ground.

questions.teachingTip: Use a hoop or some ropes to show the edges of the relief area. Let the junior practise dropping and see if the ball stays in the area.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think the ball stays where it stops, even if it is outside the relief area.
Some may want to place the ball by hand instead of dropping it again.

questions.title: What happens if the dropped ball rolls out of the relief area?
questions.question: After you drop your ball in the correct place, it rolls out of the relief area. What do you do next?

choices.text: Drop the ball again in the relief area
Place the ball where it stopped
Hit it from where it finished
Move it back to the original spot

questions.explanation: If your dropped ball comes to rest outside the relief area, you must drop it again within the relief area.
